newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares steady, seen stable to year-end.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares steady, seen stable to year-end.

text.p: Slovenian shares were little changed on Friday as profit-taking ahead of a new tax ran out of steam and market participants forecast prices would hold steady throughout the holiday season.
The 10-share SBI index rose 1.40 points to 1,162.9.
"Unless some major move or information appears, the market will remain stable until the end of the year," Andrej Ciuha, a trader at brokerage Inter Timex said.

Turnover fell to 88 million tolars from 200.1 million as business faded ahead of the new legislation, which extends a 25 percent tax on profits from securities to individuals from next year. The charge already applies to companies.
Overall eight shares rose, nine fell and eight were untraded.
Bank SKB was the most active share, firming 0.25 percent to an average 41,857 tolars on volume of 567 shares. The bank last month announced plans to list its shares on the London stock exchange.
Preferred shares of hipotekarna Bank Brezice were the biggest gainer, firming 4.23 percent to an average of 4,166 tolars on volume of 30 shares.
Brokerage Dadas was the leading decliner, falling 6.60 percent to 8,000 tolars on volume of 43 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
